files.decision: Preserve the complete upstream MIT notice.
Maintain original English documentation for this JavaScript adaptation.
Review tooling versions and keep JavaScript tooling with a local lockfile, module.js entry, and file-referenced license metadata.
Adapt the ES module build without TypeScript-only aliases; transform the language root structurally, inject Sass identity, and retain the unified src layout and per-id output.
Retain Rui Pinheiro's MIT attribution and review the deliberately limited JavaScript fallback.
Use explicit stable/prerelease publication, validate the selected commit, create its associated tag, and publish verified assets with curated release notes.
Intentionally omitted: no Discord announcements or Foundry website publication.
Keep a small entry point that imports styles and installs the lifecycle listeners.
Register JavaScript lifecycle modules centrally, including the local ready phase.
Register client settings, the ModuleApi instance, and named native-query handlers during init; no global Handlebars helper.
Read stored diagnostic settings and keep optional integration setup explicit; no core wrappers are registered by default.
Track upstream HMR changes for review; the local implementation promises rebuilding and documented reloads, not full parity.
Keep named registration and access for the real client debug setting in one JavaScript module.
Keep module-prefixed logging with local diagnostics behavior.
Intentionally omitted: localization keys are prepared in application context and templates use existing Foundry helpers; no custom global helper.
Keep literal MODULE_ID, MODULE_TITLE, and MODULE_VERSION exports validated against manifest/package metadata; derive paths and localization keys.
The upstream file contains TypeScript interfaces; the local ModuleApi class and readiness/socket contract are independent runtime implementations.
Validate the source identity against package metadata and literal constants; preserve version and the boolean socket flag, generate release URLs, and leave verified unset until runtime tests.
Preserve live packs while cleaning only a marked per-id output directory.
Link the per-id output to Foundry; refuse replacing an existing real directory.
Target only src/module.json, package.json, literal constants.js declarations, and generated package-lock root metadata; preserve other source, documentation, changelog history, and provenance.
Compile declared packs from packs-src and require explicit overwrite of existing output.
Extract compiled packs into tracked source directories with explicit overwrite handling.
Resolve declared pack names and paths for the local source/output layout.
Start an explicitly configured local Foundry installation using the chosen version.
Document local Foundry Data and versioned installation paths without committing personal configuration.

intentionalDifferences: JavaScript source, JavaScript build helpers, and JSDoc rather than TypeScript compilation.
src/module.json, src/module.js, src/lang, src/styles, src/templates, src/assets, and src/scripts.
A built module lives inside dist/<module-id>; the release ZIP preserves that directory.
Release assets are named module.json and module.zip.
Download URLs are pinned to the exact tag; stable manifests use the latest stable feed and prerelease manifests remain pinned to their own tags.
Independent Node-based ZIP packaging and verification.

No Git-history-derived release notes, pull-request workflows, scheduled checks, upstream bots, automatic merges, or Discord/Foundry website publication; release changes come from curated CHANGELOG entries.
Development uses rebuilding and documented reloads; it does not promise parity with every upstream HMR behavior.
Identity uses three explicit authored files with literal runtime constants; paths, translation namespaces, and Sass scoping derive from their validated values.
The generic settings application controls real client debug logging; no sample feature toggle or custom global Handlebars helper is registered.
ModuleApi exposes readiness and a native ModuleSocket service; the guarded module.socket alias must preserve the core boolean manifest flag and be verified in a real Foundry build.
Release workflows have no version input: the source manifest, package, literal constant, and dated changelog must agree on strict unprefixed SemVer.

localAdditions.decision: Original ModuleApi readiness and status contract, reusable client-debug settings application, and guarded runtime socket alias preserving serialized manifest data.

Original native Foundry 14 query adapter with namespaced registration, canonical caller context, explicit authorization, QUERY_USER checks, and unchanged multi-user settled results. No socketlib implementation is copied or required.
Original validation of the three authored identity files, structural language-root transformation, and targeted renaming with generated lockfile metadata.
